page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the cx family, running on the QEMU hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon CPU with 2 shared vCPUs and 2 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 40 GB NVMe SSD, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data indicates that the cx23 operates within the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1028.88 and multi-core scored 2016.78, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 149.36 GB/sec and an uncached large block write speed of 16.93 GB/sec, which ranks in the bottom 25%. Geekbench results align with these findings, yielding a single-core score of 654.0 and a multi-core score of 1177.0. For database operations, the server achieved 2.52 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and static web serving throughput reached 1.77 GB/sec. Small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model processed prompts at 169.87 tokens per second and generated text at 52.23 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the cx23 is its shared CPU allocation and entry-level resource density, which limits its capability under sustained heavy compute loads. However, this hardware profile offers high qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight applications that do not require dedicated CPU resources. The server is designed for low-demand workloads such as basic web serving, small development environments, lightweight utility scripts, and simple database testing where resource consumption remains minimal.
